business_scope.primary_industry_name: Intermodal ISO Shipping Container Fleet Asset Leasing

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Confédération suisse / Schweizerische Eidgenossenschaft / Confederazione Svizzera)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), Art. 620 ff. (Aktiengesellschaft), Art. 626 (articles of incorporation), Art. 632 (paid-in capital), Art. 697j (duty to maintain beneficial-owner records); Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0) of 10 Oct 1997, Art. 3–9 (CDD, KYC), Art. 6 (PEP enhanced due diligence), Art. 53 (suspicious activity reporting to MROS); FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA, SR 955.033) of 3 Jun 2015; Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Entities and the Identification of Beneficial Owners (Transparenzgesetz) of 22 Jun 2023, in force 1 Jul 2024; Transparency Ordinance (SR 221.433); Ordinance on the Commercial Register (HRegV, SR 221.411) of 17 Oct 2007.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each individual shareholder and each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (consular legalization only for non-Hague signatory states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or current commercial register extract of any corporate shareholder
Certified articles of association and constitutional deed of corporate founder
Notarized general or special power of attorney for incorporation and bank account opening
Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for initial share capital and fleet assets
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-official signature verification; apostille required where bank is located in a non-Hague jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories and commercial counterparties against: (1) UN Security Council sanctions regimes (1267/1989, 1988, 2253 ISIL/Da'esh); (2) OFAC SDN and consolidated non-SDN lists; (3) EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (4) Swiss SECO expor-t and financial sanctions list (situation on sanctions, embargoes); (5) FINMA enforcement and civil-law sanction registers; and (6) national PEP databases. PEPs require enhanced due diligence under AMLA Art. 6 and AMLO-FINMA Art. 20–23, including source-of-wealth documentation, senior-management approval and enhanced transaction monitoring. Suspicious activity must be reported to the Swiss Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS). For this low-risk container-leasing scope, the risk tier is Low_Risk_Standard; refresh screening at least annually and upon any change in ownership or management.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Names Index (zefix.ch); incorporation filings are submitted through the competent cantonal commercial register office (Handelsregisteramt), coordinated by the Federal Commercial Register Office (EHRA), with publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be rendered in Latin script and contain at least one official Swiss language (German, French, Italian or Romansh). The legal-form suffix must match the language of the registered name: 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' (German), 'Société Anonyme' or 'SA' (French/Italian). Free-designator terms in English or other languages are permissible only if the name is not misleading and does not violate Swiss naming doctrine (Art. 944 and Art. 950 OR; Art. 15 HRegV). Non-Latin-script names must be accompanied by a certified translation into the chosen official language.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Banca (requires FINMA licence under Banking Act Art. 1)
Insurance / Versicherung / Assurance (requires FINMA licence under Insurance Supervision Act)
Swiss / Suisse / Schweiz / Svizzera / Switzerland (requires IPI authorization under Swissness legislation, Trade Mark Protection Act Art. 47–52)
SICAV / SIF / collective-investment terms (requires CISA licence)
Canton names, municipal names or coats of arms (require cantonal consent)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Swiss law does not provide a statutory online preliminary name-clearance step; operative clearance occurs at incorporation filing, although most cantonal registers offer a non-binding preliminary name check or unilateral reservation upon fee payment for a limited window (commonly 30 days). If a name is refused, the applicant may: (1) file a revised name within the same application; (2) submit a written objection to the cantonal commercial register office within the applicable cantonal time limit, commonly 30 days; (3) appeal to the cantonal commercial-register supervisory authority; and (4) appeal to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) under the Federal Act on Administrative Procedure (VwVG) if the lower decision violates federal law. Reservations are not extendable beyond the applicable cantonal window; a fresh reservation may be filed with a variant name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permitted. The registered office must be fixed in the canton where corporate administration is actually conducted; a pure mailbox or address-provider arrangement without factual substance (Sitzgesellschaft) is tolerated only for passive holding and personal companies and is unattractive and risky for an active intermodal container-leasing undertaking under tax anti-abuse doctrine and AMLA substance expectations. For this industry, a serviced office with a verifiable Swiss operational anchor (fleet-management functions, invoicing, bookkeeping, board meeting venue, local bank account) is acceptable. Virtual office acceptance is therefore conditional on demonstrated commercial substance in Switzerland.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% probability within the first 12 months of operation; probability exceeds 20% if the same serviced-address provider hosts more than 20 corporate tenants or if cantonal tax or commercial-register authorities classify the entity as a dormant or domiciliary company.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Non-binding preliminary company-name check and reservation fee (cantonal commercial register)
Notarial certification of incorporation deed and articles of association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial tariff; prevailing market benchmark CHF 1,000–1,800

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register registration fee for incorporation of an Aktiengesellschaft
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal commercial register / EHRA federal fee share
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule per HRegV and cantonal fee tariff; approx. CHF 600–900

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
Statutory minimum share capital deposit in blocked bank account (Art. 621 and Art. 632 OR) – capitalizable, not a fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Mandatory capitalization: CHF 100,000 minimum; paid-in at least 20% but typically 100% for an active leasing entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of shareholder and UBO document bundle (3–5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-country competent authority (Hague Convention) or Swiss consular post where required
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee tariff; approx. CHF 60–120 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign-language corporate and identity documents into German, French or Italian
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark CHF 0.20–0.30 per translated line; CHF 80–150 per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO identification file compilation and KYC dossier (Art. 697j OR; Transparenzgesetz)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Swiss corporate service provider or fiduciary

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP / OFAC / UN / SECO sanctions screening tool annual subscription
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark CHF 700–1,000 per annum for low-volume SME

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office provision and corporate secretarial services (12 months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed fiduciary or service provider in canton of registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss corporate bank account opening fee (SWIFT wire and ACH debit rails)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Swiss bank (e.g., UBS, ZKB, Raiffeisen)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Fiduciary incorporation package and legal project management fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark CHF 3,000–5,000 for standard AG incorporation with UBO analysis

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht), Articles 626–642 (incorporation of the Aktiengesellschaft), Articles 716a–716b (non-transferable board powers), and Article 627 (registered office and corporate purpose); Federal Act on the Commercial Register (Handelsregisterverordnung) Articles 1, 14, and 18.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), administered under the cantonal Department for Economic Affairs; federal supervision by the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Authority.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsakt) executed before a Swiss notary public, followed by the Application for Registration in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of CHF 100,000 (approx. USD 112,000); at least CHF 50,000 must be fully paid up in cash before registration; contribution must be deposited in an escrow account at a Swiss bank, blocked in favour of the company, and released upon completion of registration; in-kind contributions require an audit report confirming the value of contributed assets.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The board of directors of this Swiss Aktiengesellschaft, having received the certificate of incorporation, hereby resolves: first, to confirm and accept the subscription of all shares, including the in-cash and in-kind contributions, and to approve the allocation of shares to each shareholder; second, to adopt the registered office at the principal place of business in the Canton of Zug; third, to appoint the first board of directors and the managing director, with the managing director holding sole individual signatory authority; fourth, to open a corporate bank account for the deposit of paid-up capital and future operations; and fifth, to authorize and instruct the directors to take all necessary steps to effect this resolution. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public authorized in the Canton of Zug, Switzerland
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a fully licensed Swiss notary to draft the Deed of Incorporation (Statuten) in compliance with the Swiss Code of Obligations. The deed must include: corporate name, registered office (address in Zug), corporate purpose limited to international intermodal ISO container leasing and related logistics assets, share capital amount (minimum CHF 100,000), nominal value and classes of shares, number of directors, and publication organ. All founders must appear before the notary personally or by written power of attorney; passport, proof of address, and proof of deposit of paid-up capital (blocked account) must be presented. The notary verifies identity and legal capacity, then reads the deed and accepts the signatures of all founders. The notary retains the original and issues certified copies for the commercial register process.
required_dossiers: Statutes (Articles of Association) drafted in German or English
Foundation deed (Errichtungsakt) signed by all founders
Passport or identity card of each founder
Proof of residence or domicile of each founder
Blocked account certificate from a Swiss bank confirming deposit of CHF 50,000 minimum
Power of attorney (if a representative signs on behalf of any founder)
Report of a licensed auditor for any in-kind contributions (Sacheinlageprüfung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies deficiencies in the draft deed (e.g., incomplete corporate purpose clauses or lack of designation of the registered office), remedy by amending the deed text and re-executing before the same notary; no new notarial appointment is required if the same notary handles the file. If the notary refuses execution due to unlawful object or procedural default, submit a revised draft within 5 business days or file a formal objection with the Cantonal Commercial Register Authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Paid-Up Capital Escrow Deposit and Bank Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank or financial intermediary (e.g., cantonal bank or private bank) operating under Swiss banking supervision (FINMA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the name of the future company at a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank. Deposit the minimum paid-up capital of CHF 50,000 (cash portion) into the blocked account. Obtain the bank's written confirmation of the blocking arrangement and the identity of the account holder, together with proof of the deposit. The bank must release funds only upon presentation of the commercial registry certificate of registration. If share capital is contributed in kind, obtain a licensed Swiss audit firm's report (Revisionsstelle) on the valuation of the contributed assets, such as a container fleet or lease portfolio. The audit report must accompany the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Application form for opening the escrow account
Statutory draft of the future company
Passport existing for each founding shareholder
Beneficial ownership declaration (Form A)
Bank due diligence questionnaire
Proof of source of funds
Audit report on in-kind contributions (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening due to KYC deficiencies, provide complete source-of-funds evidence and a Swiss residence or business nexus, or switch to another FINMA-supervised bank (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank). If the blocked account certificate fails to meet the Commercial Register requirements, demand a corrected certificate specifying the account holder, deposit date, and blocking clause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Commercial Register Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Application for Registration (Anmeldung) to the Commercial Register Office of Zug, attaching the notarized deed of incorporation, the certified copy of the statutes, the bank blocked-account certificate, and the registered office declaration signed by the board and the person authorized to represent the company for registration. Sign the application before the Commercial Register Officer or by notarized electronic signature. The filing must be made in electronic form through the e-Register portal (e-register.ch) or in paper form; if made electronically, the document must be accompanied by a QR-scannable cover sheet and the notary's certification. Pay the cantonal registration fee (approximately CHF 400–800) via bank transfer or direct debit.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and statutes
Application form (Anmeldung) signed by the board
Blocked account certificate from Swiss bank
Audit report on in-kind contributions (if any)
Declaration of registered office address
List of directors and authorized signatories with passport copies
Consent declarations of all members of the board
Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register issues a query or suspension order, cure the defect within the 20-day statutory deadline by submitting the missing documents, correcting formal errors, or clarifying the corporate name or registered office. A formal appeal can be lodged with the Cantonal Court after the deadline if the rejection is final.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of the review, the Commercial Register registers the company and issues an extract from the Commercial Register (Handelsregister-Auszug) confirming the legal existence of the Aktiengesellschaft. The evidence of incorporation includes: company name, legal form (Aktiengesellschaft), registered office in Zug, share capital, board members, and signature modalities (e.g., one signature if so designated). The certificate is electronically retrievable from the official e-Register portal. The registration is published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB).
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration issued by the Commercial Register
Extract from the Commercial Register (Handelsregister-Auszug)
Official publication notice in the SHAB
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the register entry contains factual errors (e.g., incorrect share capital or name), file a rectification application with the Commercial Register Officer, supported by the notarial deed and notary's certificate. If the certificate is delayed, request a progress note from the cantonal register and, if necessary, escalate to the cantonal supervisory authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Organizational Board Resolution and Mandatory Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Aktiengesellschaft (recorded in minutes, notarially certified copies may be needed for bank and third parties)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a formal board meeting immediately after incorporation. Adopt the incumbent board resolution covering: (i) ratification of the articles of association; (ii) election of the chairman and managing director; (iii) adoption of the registered office address; (iv) opening of the company bank account with the released escrowed funds; (v) appointment of the independent auditing body (Revisionsstelle) if required for a capital above CHF 500,000 or due to the scope of activities, otherwise an express waiver of the limited review (Luzern) with a declaration; and (vi) authorization of the managing director to execute lease agreements, bank documentation, and operational contracts in connection with the ISO container leasing business. Minutes must be signed by all board members and kept in the company's corporate records.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
Board resolution on appointments and authorization
Certificate of incorporation issued by the Commercial Register
List of shareholders and share register
Written acceptance declarations of all board members
Declaration of the registered office
Application for removal of the blocked account restriction to the releasing bank
Application for VAT registration (VAT number) with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to release the escrowed capital without the board resolution, obtain a notarized excerpt of the minutes. If an internal deadlock or disagreement arises among directors, resubmit the resolution to an extraordinary general meeting and obtain a simple majority or unanimous vote as required by the articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Indirect Tax Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung - ESTV) and Cantonal Tax Administration of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Swiss VAT number (UID / MWST) by submitting the registration form electronically to the ESTV, using the registration portal or the Swiss Federal Tax Administration's online service. For a container leasing company, note that the leasing of transport containers is generally subject to VAT at the standard rate of 8.1%; but cross-border leasing may be exempt or zero-rated if the container is used outside Switzerland, requiring documentary evidence and periodic VAT returns. Register with the cantonal tax office for direct federal tax, cantonal corporate income tax, and cantonal capital tax. The Zug cantonal tax administration will issue a tax number and integrate the taxpayer into the tax assessment cycle. Sign an agreement for electronic submission of tax returns and annual financial statements.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract
Certificate of incorporation
Board resolution confirming tax registration
Bank details for refunds and payments
Document supporting foreign use of containers (for cross-border leasing)
VAT registration form (SIF Form)
Application for cantonal tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT registration is delayed or rejected for lack of documents, resubmit the complete set and, if needed, request an advance ruling from the ESTV on the place of supply of container leasing services. For cantonal tax objections, file a formal objection with the Zug Tax Office and obtain an assessment order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer Registration and Social Security Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zug Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse des Kantons Zug) and Swiss Accident Insurance Fund (Suva) for mandatory accident insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the company hires employees in Switzerland, register as an employer with the Zug cantonal compensation office (Ausgleichskasse) within 3 business days after hire. Obtain the employer registration number for AHV/IV/EO contributions (old-age, survivors, and disability insurance) and apply to Suva for mandatory accident insurance coverage. For a container leasing company with staff only abroad, Swiss employer registration is optional but may still be required for a Swiss administrative office. Submit completed registration forms, employee details, and payroll data to the compensation office.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract
List of employees with passport and residence permits
Registration form for AHV (Formular AHV)
Employer registration form of the Compensation Office
Application for accident insurance with Suva
Board resolution confirming the payroll and HR policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the compensation office challenges the employer classification or contribution period, provide personnel records and employment contracts; appeal to the Cantonal Social Security Authority within 30 days if the ruling is unfavorable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Corporate Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by FINMA (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank, UBS, Credit Suisse, or an innovative bank offering corporate accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the commercial register entry, submit the corporate bank account opening application to the chosen Swiss bank. Provide the bank with: certificate of incorporation, commercial register extract, board resolution approving the account, articles of association, beneficial owner declarations, source of funds information, and confirmation that the account is intended for the container leasing business. Meet the bank's compliance officer in person or via a secure video call. The bank performs a comprehensive due diligence review, including the verification of the beneficial owner, the intended business model, and the economic purpose of the leasing operations. The bank may request a detailed business plan and a projection of container leasing revenue and expenses.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract and certificate of incorporation
Articles of association
Board resolution on account opening
Beneficial owner declaration (Form A and Form I)
Passport and residence permit of directors and ultimate beneficial owners
Business plan for container leasing operations (asset and fleet description)
Source of funds declaration for initial capital
Internal KYC questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank downgrades the account due to a perceived high-risk jurisdiction of a client or a lack of local substance, strengthen the business plan and provide evidence of a Swiss physical presence (office lease in Zug, administrative personnel, and management). If the bank formally rejects the application, apply to a second bank, using the same network of commercial desks. The approval process may take longer for a container leasing company because the ISIC 5229 code is not considered high-risk under Swiss anti-money laundering regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Office for Economic Affairs and Labour of Zug (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit) and the Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN) if any warehouse or containers are stored on Swiss soil
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific operating license is required for intermodal leasing purely as an asset-leasing activity under Swiss federal law; however, if storage or depots are operated, a cantonal industrial operation permit (Betriebsbewilligung) may be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN) and Canton of Zug Environmental Protection Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Registration (Exempt from full EIA report) for container storage yards below 5,000 square meters and with no hazardous waste handling; full EIA required only if the facility exceeds relevant thresholds under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV, SR 814.011)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Swiss Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV) for any discharge, zero liquid effluents from storage and cleaning operations, VOC emissions below the threshold of 0.2 kg/h or 200 kg/year in case of painting and maintenance activities, waste disposal through certified waste management operators in accordance with the Ordinance on the Movements of Waste (VEVA), and noise protection under the Noise Abatement Ordinance (LSV).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Zug Cantonal Fire Brigade, structural load certification for any container storage racks, and workplace clearance from the Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (Suva) for any offices or storage facilities; all facilities must receive a fire protection certificate before use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des impôts AFD / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC); e-portal at www.estv.admin.ch, including the dedicated VAT online services portal (VAT-Online) for registration, filing, assessments, and refund applications.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Swiss Aktiengesellschaft in the cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregister / Registre du commerce); the Federal Statistical Office automatically allocates the Swiss Business Identification Number (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, UID, format CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx) upon registration. Step 2: The AG must separately register for VAT with ESTV if its worldwide turnover from taxable supplies exceeds CHF 100,000 per calendar year; registration is filed electronically through the ESTV VAT portal using the official registration form and becomes effective retroactively to the commencement of the taxable activity. Step 3: For a foreign-controlled AG, the statutory VAT identification is the UID followed by the MWST/TVA/IVA suffix (for example CHE-116.037.634 MWST); foreign enterprises without a Swiss registered seat must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative and provide a Swiss service address before the UID/VAT number can be activated. Step 4: The UID must be shown on all invoices, customs declarations, and business correspondence, and must be renewed or derecognised only through the official Swiss business register platforms.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the Aktiengesellschaft is a resident corporate taxpayer with unlimited tax liability on worldwide commercial profit at federal, cantonal, and communal levels. Income and capital gains derived through a foreign permanent establishment or from foreign real estate are allocatively exempt in most double tax treaties and, unilaterally, benefit from income allocation rules; no pass-through status is available; the AG remains a separately taxed legal entity notwithstanding 100% foreign shareholding.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election or elective hybrid-mismatch regime exists in Swiss federal tax law. Available elections and statutory mechanisms relevant to an AG: (1) VAT group election under Art. 12 VAT Act allowing financially, economically, and organisationally interconnected Swiss enterprises to file as a single taxable person; (2) profit and loss transfer agreement (Organschaft) under Art. 733b Code of Obligations for income-tax consolidation; (3) cantonal tax status elections such as mixed company or domicile company status where the relevant canton grants reduced cantonal taxation of foreign-source income; (4) patent box election under Art. 24b of the Tax Harmonisation Act (valid in cantons adopting the IP box); (5) notional interest deduction election on excess equity in cantons that have legislated it; (6) election under Art. 34 VAT Act to compute VAT on received consideration (cash accounting basis) where annual VAT turnover does not exceed CHF 5 million; and (7) voluntary VAT registration by a below-threshold or foreign-only-supply business in order to claim input VAT deduction rights.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of taxable turnover per calendar year (Art. 10 VAT Act, threshold reduced on 1 January 2019). For foreign businesses, registration is required only when turnover sourced from Swiss territory exceeds CHF 100,000 annually; voluntary registration is permitted for enterprises that make exclusively zero-rated or export supplies in order to recover input VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping regime for VAT. Taxpaying entities must submit VAT returns electronically through the ESTV VAT portal, but invoices remain contract-based instruments under the Code of Obligations. Mandatory electronic billing is limited to the healthcare sector (health insurers and medical service providers), with full obligation phased in by end of 2026. Market-standard structured e-invoicing uses the Swiss eBill framework based on the SIX QR-bill and Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 formats; ESR/ISR payment slips remain accepted. An invoice issued by a Swiss lessor to a foreign customer must contain the supplier UID, the customer foreign VAT/TIN number where available, the date of supply, the description of the leased ISO containers, and either the affirmation not subject to Swiss VAT (place of supply abroad) or the 0% export rate, as applicable under the VAT Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Container fleet leasing qualifies for Swiss export zero-rating through two routes: (i) Supply of goods, Art. 23 VAT Act: the lease of containers constitutes an export supply only where economic ownership or the goods themselves are physically dispatched abroad and the supplier holds conclusive proof of removal from Swiss customs territory; the supply is taxed at 0% and the input VAT deduction on related costs is fully preserved. (ii) Supply of services, Art. 7(1) VAT Act: leasing of movable tangible property (ISO shipping containers) to a business customer whose seat or permanent establishment is outside Switzerland is deemed to take place at the customer's location, thereby falling outside the Swiss territorial scope and being invoiced without Swiss VAT (fiscally equivalent to 0%). Eligibility requires contemporaneous written evidence: the lessee's foreign business registration and TIN, the lease agreement with container box numbers, transport documentation for cross-border movements, and proof that the container is not used for a supply subject to Swiss VAT. The Swiss lessor must also retain lease invoices and lease schedules for the VAT retention period of ten years. Input VAT refunds on costs allocable to these export supplies (fuel, maintenance, financing, logistics) are claimed by set-off in the regular Swiss VAT return, or through the simplified ESTV refund procedure for foreign companies not established in Switzerland, subject to reciprocity and the statutory substantiation documents.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss customs export declaration (Ausfuhranmeldung / déclaration en douane d'exportation) lodged electronically in the e-dec or e-dec web system of the Federal Customs Administration (OZD), including the container item codes and harmonised codes.
Bill of Lading, sea waybill, CMR consignment note, or air waybill evidencing movement of the leased containers out of the Swiss customs territory.
Commercial lease agreement and lease schedule identifying the intermodal FCL container box numbers and the foreign lessee's registered address and VAT identification.
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank credit statement or SWIFT confirmation) evidencing collection of lease rental proceeds from the foreign lessee.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ESTV audits export-zero-rating and place-of-supply claims through on-site review and documentary request procedures. If the evidence bundle is incomplete, contradictory, or fraudulent, the tax authority retrospectively recharges Swiss VAT at 8.1% on the full lease rental for the entire statutory assessment period of ten years, adds statutory default interest currently fixed at 5% per annum under Art. 36(4) VAT Act, and may impose administrative penalty assessments under Art. 58 VAT Act of up to three times the evaded VAT. Where the exporter submits forged telexes, false bills of lading, or sham lease agreements, criminal proceedings under the Swiss Penal Code (forgery of documents, punishable imprisonment up to five years) and the aggravated tax evasion provisions of the VAT Act apply, including monetary fines up to CHF 30,000. Switzerland maintains no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline or capital control procedure; the 180-day benchmark is the conventional documentary standard applied by Swiss banks and the ESTV to evidence genuine payment flows in cross-border leasing transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 turnover per calendar year (Art. 10 VAT Act; for foreign businesses, CHF 100,000 of turnover sourced from Swiss territory). Voluntary registration is permitted for entities supplying only zero-rated or non-subject services in order to recover input VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control requirement applies under Swiss VAT law. VAT returns must be filed electronically through the ESTV VAT portal. Mandatory e-billing is limited to the healthcare sector (insurance carriers and medical service providers, fully mandatory from 2026). Standard commercial practice uses Swiss eBill / QR-bill and Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 formats for B2B e-invoicing, but paper invoices remain legally valid. Cross-border container leasing invoices must contain the supplier UID, customer foreign VAT identification, lease details, and either a zero-rating note or a statement that the place of supply is abroad.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Leasing of ISO shipping containers is treated as a service related to movable tangible property located at the customer's seat under Art. 7(3)(f) VAT Act (B2B rule). Where the lessee is established abroad, the supply falls outside the Swiss territorial scope; the Swiss lessor applies 0% output tax and retains the full input VAT deduction on costs, provided it holds documentary proof of the customer's foreign seat and container deployment abroad. Export of containers as goods with physical removal from Swiss customs territory qualifies for 0% zero-rating under Art. 23 VAT Act only upon customs-verified export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss customs export declaration (Ausfuhranmeldung) filed in the e-dec customs clearance system of the Federal Customs Administration (EZV)
Bill of Lading (or CMR/AWB) evidencing physical removal from Switzerland
Commercial lease agreement and lease schedule identifying the FCL container box numbers and the foreign lessee
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank credit confirmation) evidencing receipt of lease rental proceeds from the foreign lessee
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ESTV and cantonal audit authorities scrutinize export evidence and place-of-supply documentation. Non-substantiated zero-rating is retrospectively reversed with VAT assessed on the gross rental for up to ten years, plus statutory default interest at 5% p.a. (Art. 36(4) VAT Act). Deliberate VAT evasion triggers penalty surcharges of up to three times the evaded tax (Art. 58 VAT Act) and criminal fines up to CHF 30,000; forged documents (e.g., false Bills of Lading, simulated inward remittances) are prosecuted under the Swiss Criminal Code (Art. 251, art. 252 and 314a) with imprisonment up to five years. Switzerland has no general foreign-exchange control; the 180-day repatriation period is a documentary benchmark rather than a statutory capital-control deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB), established under the Federal Act on the Swiss National Bank (SNB Act, SR 951.11), is the sole monetary and exchange-rate authority; foreign-exchange controls, balance-of-payments reporting, and statistical notification obligations are codified under the Foreign Exchange Ordinance (SR 941.141). Banking conduct supervision is co-executed with the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland grants full currency convertibility on both current and capital accounts. The Swiss franc is freely convertible; there are no general exchange-control approvals, no withholding limitations on the transfer of lease rental income, no restrictions on dividend cross-border payment, and no impediments to capital repatriation by non-resident shareholders, provided that Swiss anti-money-laundering rules and the statutory 35% withholding tax on dividends are observed. The 35% dividend tax can be reduced or refunded under an applicable double-taxation treaty or under the Swiss Notification Procedure for treaty relief. A Swiss AG engaged in intermodal ISO container leasing may hold USD, EUR, CNY, and other convertible receivables in foreign-currency current accounts without any SNB licence or FX allocation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender obligation exists. Switzerland imposes no statutory repatriation timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts; the container-leasing company may retain lease proceeds indefinitely in any freely convertible currency or offshore. Only the statistical reporting regime of SR 941.141 applies, under which payments exceeding CHF 50,000 may be selected for sample-based balance-of-payments reporting, which is purely informational and does not constitute an approval, conversion, or surrender requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium for low-value operational treasury functions; Low for serving as the capital escrow account or as the primary trade-settlement institution. Legal constraints: the EU/EEA financial services passport does not extend to Switzerland, so a foreign electronic money institution must either hold or route funds through a Swiss banking partner or apply for a FINMA fintech licence under Art. 1b para 2 of the Banking Act, which caps public deposits at CHF 100 million and prohibits interest business and maturity transformation. For a cross-border leasing treasury, the compliant architecture is a Swiss commercial bank core account for escrow, SWIFT settlements and letters of credit, with an EMI used only for small-value disbursements, expenses, and multi-currency operational float.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory for at least one director with individual signature rights. Swiss banks require an onboarding interview at the bank's physical premises; some major banks accept a FINMA-regulated secured video identification procedure for corporate clients, but fully remote onboarding without any interview is generally rejected for a newly formed Swiss AG with cross-border trade counterparties. Required documentation includes the certified Commercial Register excerpt, notarised articles of incorporation, UBO declaration with source-of-wealth evidence for every natural person holding more than 25%, board resolutions appointing banking signatories, and, where applicable, the notarised capital-increase deed executed under Art. 650 of the Swiss Code of Obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in ultimate beneficial ownership: nominee shareholdings, shell intermediate entities, or trusts without transparent economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO register per Art. 3 AMLA; notarised declarations of beneficial ownership; corporate chart from the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregister); audited financial statements; bank reference letters from any prior banking relationships; and a capitalisation trail with source-of-funds evidence from each contributing shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing economic substance in Switzerland: virtual office, no employees, absent directors, and no AHV or social security registrations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed physical office lease; payroll and AHV accident insurance certificates; Swiss UID tax identification; director residence permits; substance minutes evidencing day-to-day container asset management, fleet documentation, lease contracts, and maintenance-depot agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate inbound lump-sum capital injection not aligned with the lease portfolio size or the company's stated turnover.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital-increase deed under Art. 650 OR; extraordinary general meeting minutes; bank statements from the contributing shareholder covering the source of funds; source-of-wealth declarations; and independent valuation or purchase invoices for container assets funded by the contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or from high-risk trade counterparties, freight forwarders, or container depot operators in jurisdictions subject to enhanced due diligence or sanctions scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master container lease agreements and depot storage agreements; bills of lading and delivery receipts; KYC packs for each institutional lessee and industrial counterparty; know-your-supplier documentation; and an automated sanctions and adverse-media screening log maintained after account opening.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound subscription and capital-increase funds must be routed by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the shareholder's own bank account into the Swiss company's escrowed capital account. The payment narrative and ISO 20022 purpose code (e.g., EQUI, Equity capital) must reference the subscription resolution, the company's Swiss UID number, and its Handelsregister identification number. Supporting documentation comprises the notarised capital-increase deed under Art. 650 OR, the extraordinary general meeting minutes, and the updated Commercial Register filing; the CHF 100,000 statutory minimum capital must remain unencumbered until final registration. No SNB approval is required, but the bank submits statistical balance-of-payments notifications under SR 941.141 for inflows exceeding CHF 50,000 when sampled. Inbound USD or EUR wires are traced via SWIFT gpi with UETR and may be converted to CHF at the bank's spot rate, or held in a multi-currency capital account where the capital increase so provides.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing is anchored on SWIFT MT103 wire transfers with UETR tracking for lease settlements, container purchase payments to PRC or Korean box manufacturers, and depot and maintenance disbursements. Irrevocable commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 are the standard rail for new container manufacturing payments, complemented by documentary collections under URC 522 for used-container resales. Same-day CHF payments are effected through the Swiss Payments Platform (SPP); euro-denominated flows clear through SEPA; for recurring domestic CHF collections, the LSV+ direct-debit rail (the Swiss ACH equivalent) is applicable, whereas the North American ACH-debit rail is limited to client debits in the United States. Multi-currency current accounts enable per-currency pooling; surplus USD receivables are swept by standing instructions and converted or hedged as set out below.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright vanilla FX forwards up to 12-month tenors with Swiss banking counterparties (UBS AG, ZKB, BCV) to fix the CHF conversion price of USD lease-rental inflows
Non-deliverable CNY forwards (NDFs) to hedge the USD/CNY mismatch on container box purchases from PRC manufacturers when settlement must reference the onshore CNY fix

Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement together with the Swiss Master Agreement for standby liquidity, converting surplus USD cash into CHF at tenors matched to the container lease portfolio

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal and cantonal corporate income tax return (Steuererklärung), including net wealth/capital tax statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) and competent cantonal tax authority of the canton of registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after close of fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, normally by 30 June of the following year, unless an extension is granted.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The tax authority may issue an estimated assessment if the return is omitted; default interest accrues (federal direct tax currently 4.0% p.a.; cantonal rate varies), late-filing fines up to CHF 10,000 apply, and enforcement measures may be commenced.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss value added tax (VAT/GST) return (Mehrwertsteuerabrechnung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each reporting period; annual reporters generally file by late February/early March after the calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission triggers reminder surcharge and default interest at the statutory VAT rate; continued failure allows the VAT authority to determine the tax by estimation, plus administrative penalties of up to CHF 8,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer social security declaration and contribution statement (AHV wage declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent cantonal compensation office (Ausgleichskasse); SUVA for occupational accident insurance where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 28 February for the prior calendar year; interim declarations on quarterly or monthly payroll periods as prescribed by the compensation office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or underestimation leads to an assessed contribution, default interest on late employer contributions, reminder costs, and administrative or criminal sanctions for wage concealment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, sign-off by directors) and approval by shareholders at the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No governmental filing; the approved statements must be retained at the registered office and audited financial statements placed before the shareholders' meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must be held within 6 months after the balance sheet date; for a 31 December balance sheet, no later than 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the meeting is not timely held, the board may be called by the commercial register office to remedy the default; directors may be liable in damages, and a court may order judicial liquidation in cases of serious corporate governance failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial register updates and declarations (Zefix/SHAB) for any changes to directors, share capital, share transfers, registered office or corporate purpose
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven; each reportable change must be lodged within 3 months of the underlying corporate action. There is no fixed annual filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The commercial register office may impose administrative fines (Ordnungsbusse) for non-reporting; late filings may also prejudice the effectiveness of the change and expose directors to personal liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Swiss Stock Corporation (AG) must submit to an ordinary statutory audit if, in two consecutive fiscal years, it exceeds at least two of the following criteria: balance sheet total CHF 20 million; annual sales revenue CHF 40 million; 250 full-time employees. Even below those thresholds, a limited audit is required if shareholders holding at least 10% of the voting rights so request; a small AG with fewer than 10 full-time employees may waive audit entirely upon unanimous shareholder consent under Art. 727a CO.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual accounts must be prepared in accordance with the accounting provisions of the Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO, Art. 957-963) applying the recognised Swiss accounting framework (Swiss GAAP FER for SMEs); IFRS is permitted for consolidated or listed reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not maintain an annual UBO confirmation registry for commercial AGs. Non-listed companies may only issue registered shares; bearer shares are prohibited for unlisted companies. The obligation is to keep an accurate share register and to identify the beneficial owner where transfers occur or where anti-money laundering customer due diligence applies. No government annual UBO form is due.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholder register / Aktienbuch) showing registered shareholders and, where applicable, voting percentages
Register of Directors (board members and authorised signatories as recorded in the Commercial Register)
Minute Book (shareholders' meeting and board meeting signed minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,200-8,800 per year for registered-office provision and professional corporate secretarial assistance (typical CHF-equivalent rates; Zug/Zurich/Geneva at the upper range)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000-16,000 for a small or medium container-leasing AG preparing Swiss GAAP financial statements; a full ordinary audit for a company above the SME threshold may range from USD 15,000-45,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions

approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
